verifications.note: Kentucky Municipal Energy Agency 2023 resource plan, approved by its board in January 2025. Page 14 of the executive summary (PDF page 36) and Section 15, Plan 4 (PDF page 435) describe a 92 MW engine plant called KYMEA Energy Center II and a second option that grows KYMEA Energy Center I from 75 MW to 129 MW.

records.monitor_reason: The agency's 2023 resource plan studies two gas engine options for after June 2029, when its coal and peaker contracts end: a new 92 MW plant called KYMEA Energy Center II, or growing KYMEA Energy Center I from 75 MW to 129 MW. The board has not picked either one.
records.researcher_notes: The Kentucky Municipal Energy Agency 2023 resource plan is at https://s3.amazonaws.com/kymea-twill/4031257f-39bb-4be9-99b8-87cfeaf6cff8/2025_06_IRP2023-Report-Draft-v.24_6_05_25.pdf. The board approved it in January 2025. Page 14 of the executive summary (PDF page 36) lists five long-term plans. It says: "The RICE Plan calls for KYMEA to build KYMEA Energy Center II. A 92 MW greenfield RICE Plant." It also says: "The RICE | BESS Plan calls for KYMEA to expand KYMEA Energy Center I from 75 MW to 129 MW." That would add about 54 MW of engines at the Madisonville site. Section 15, Plan 4 (PDF page 435) repeats the 92 MW figure. Section 16.2 (PDF pages 452 to 455) says the board has only chosen the near-term step, KYMEA Energy Center I with four 18.8 MW engines. GEM already has that plant as unit G100001031363 under construction for 2027. No site, permit or board vote was found for either long-term option. Both are options in a study, so neither is added yet. Recheck at the agency's next resource plan or any board vote on the post-2029 supply. If the expansion is chosen, it becomes a new unit at plant L100001026095.

records.plant_name: Henderson Municipal Power & Light engine plant (plan option)

verifications.note: Henderson Municipal Power & Light 2026 resource plan, written by 1898 & Co. and dated March 31, 2026, posted by the Hendersonian news site. Table 5 (PDF page 23) shows a 36 MW engine plant in 2030 in four of five cases. Section 6 (PDF page 29) recommends starting development work now.

records.monitor_reason: Henderson's 2026 resource plan recommends a 36 MW gas engine plant for about 2030, under the 50 MW add threshold. The plan says more engines could later be added at the same site, and it also studies buying a 79 MW share of a larger combustion turbine plant around 2036.
records.researcher_notes: The Henderson Municipal Power & Light 2026 resource plan is at https://the-hendersonian.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/HMPL-2026-IRP-Report.pdf. It was written by 1898 & Co. and is dated March 31, 2026. Table 5 on PDF page 23 shows "RICE (36MW)" in 2030 in four of the five cases. The same table shows a 79 MW share of an F-class simple cycle gas turbine in 2036, and more 36 MW engines in 2036 to 2045 in the high load case. Section 6 on PDF page 29 says: "the recommended near-term action plan is for HMP&L to begin development work now on dispatchable thermal resource options targeted for the 2030 timeframe." It also says engines could later be expanded "at the same site". No site, permit or city vote was found. At 36 MW the engine plant is under the 50 MW add threshold. Recheck at the next plan update or any city utility board vote. Add it if the site reaches 50 MW, or add the 79 MW share as an owner on the larger plant once that plant is named. The copy found is posted by a local news site. A web search on November 6, 2026 found no copy on the utility's own site.
